subject: EdgeFin: fast-path SSE handshake & packet cadence — next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marek Kowalski <marek.kowalski@edgefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeFin: fast-path SSE handshake & packet cadence — next steps

Hi Marek — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance SLOs and the pilot test plan.

Call highlights (high level)
- Primary requirement: TTFT for interactive workflow (short prompts) under 75ms tail (p95) when traffic is routed through EU region.
- Throughput target: sustained 120 requests/sec for peak windows, up to 500 rps burst with autoscaling.
- Streaming: you prefer SSE for browser clients, but will accept WebSocket fallback for mobile clients behind flaky networks.
- Chunk cadence: small initial chunk (<= 64B) for heartbeat + subsequent 128–512 token chunks; client wants consistent first emission followed by steady chunk cadence to avoid rebuffer.

Proposed acceptance criteria for pilot (concrete)
1) TTFT: p95 <= 75ms on 90% of test prompts (mix provided in Drive link).
2) First chunk size & behavior: first chunk must arrive within 60–80ms and contain either an initial token bundle or heartbeat frame to unblock UI.
3) Stable cadence: after first chunk, median inter-chunk spacing <= 50ms for the first 1s of emission on streaming baseline.
4) Concurrency: system must sustain 120 rps sustained with a 10% error budget at p99.
5) Fallback: documented behavior when SSE connection falls back to WebSocket (connect+resume semantics).

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix and packetization diagram (edgefin-slo-matrix.xlsx, packet-cadence-diagram.png).

Next steps I propose:
- Your team to confirm the test prompt set and preferred client platforms (browser/mobile).
- Redwood to provision a small EU pilot cluster (dedicated slice) and run a 48h load window with telemetry.
- Tech sync with Lauren and Rishi to finalize chunk framing and handshake details — suggest Wed 18th 10:00 CET.

If any of the acceptance criteria above look off, tell me which to tune. I'll loop in our infra lead (Rishi) to own the pilot runbook once we confirm.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: EdgeFin: fast-path SSE handshake & packet cadence — next steps

Thanks Mina — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT target: 75ms p95 is acceptable, but for small prompts (<= 32 tokens) we'd like p50 <= 40ms if achievable. That's where the UI feels instant.
- Chunk cadence: the product team is worried about initial buffering on low-bandwidth mobile. If the first chunk is just a heartbeat we still need a guaranteed first token within 120ms for mobile.
- Concurrency: the 120 rps baseline is correct; however our internal e2e will simulate 10 concurrent users each doing 3 rps sustained during the session, so please size for multiplexing within one connection where possible.

We can confirm the prompt set by EOD Thursday. Wed 18th 10:00 CET works for a technical sync. For procurement: procurement will want a short pilot agreement covering data handling and retention — I will have our legal send a template.

Best,

Subject: Re: EdgeFin: fast-path SSE handshake & packet cadence — next steps

Hi Marek / Team — following up from the sync and Mina's notes. Technical plan and what we'll run during the 48h pilot: 

1) Handshake behavior\- We will implement an SSE handshake that emits an immediate small ‘meta’ frame (~30–60B) as the first emission to unblock browser UIs. That frame will be followed by either: (a) the first semantic token (if generation is ready) or (b) a heartbeat token. For mobile clients we will ensure a WebSocket resume path that allows a quick reconnect and a single-shot first-token delivery.

2) Priming & cache warmup\- We'll run a warmstart with the agreed prompt set for 30 minutes before the measured window to populate KV cache and model warm weights. This reduces cold-start TTFT variance for p95.

3) Chunk cadence tuning\- Baseline: initial chunk + 256-token chunks with target median inter-chunk spacing <= 45ms for the first 1s. We'll test a 128-token cadence in a secondary run to check client rebuffer.

4) Observability & gating\- Telemetry we will capture: TTFT (client-observed and server-side), inter-chunk timing, per-connection multiplexing stats, and queueing delays. We will provide a dashboard link (shared after run).

5) Acceptance gating\- Pass if p95 TTFT <= 75ms and mobile first-token observed <= 120ms for >= 90% of sessions, with error rates under 1% during steady-state.

Logistics: Rishi will own the runbook and post results. Mina will coordinate the client instrumentation. Ben — once Marek’s procurement sends the template we can attach the pilot order form to the DocuSign link we shared.

--
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
